caption: A lit candle in a holder is tilted to one side, and the flame keeps pointing straight up while melted wax runs down the low side.

sa.check: A lit candle in a holder is tilted to one side.
The flame keeps pointing straight up.
Melted wax runs down the candle's low side.
The wax drips off the low edge.
The flame does not lean with the candle.
The tilt comes first and the running follows.

pc.expect: The flame stays upright whatever the candle's angle and the melted wax runs down the low side and drips from its lowest point.
pc.fail: The flame leans with the candle and stays in line with the wick; or the wax runs up toward the candle's high side; or a drip leaves the candle and rises; or the wax gathers on the high side and stays there.

pc.expect: The tilt shows in the wax: the pool at the top runs toward the low side and spills there.
pc.fail: The candle tilts and the wax pool stays square with the candle's top instead of level with the ground; or the wax pool spills over the high side; or the candle tilts and no wax moves at all; or wax runs down a side the candle is not tilted toward.

pc.expect: The run only advances down the low side and stops where it sets, and set wax stays set.
pc.fail: A set run turns liquid again with no fresh wax reaching it; or the run retreats up the candle; or the candle grows taller as the wax runs; or the run advances and withdraws in turn.

pc.expect: The wax is a thin liquid near the flame that stiffens into a dull ridge lower down, and the candle's body stays a solid column.
pc.fail: The candle's body bends with the tilt; or the wax runs off as thin as water and leaves no ridge; or the run sets as a spike standing out sideways; or the candle melts through at its middle.

pc.expect: One candle with one wick and one flame in one holder; the flame stays on the wick.
pc.fail: The flame separates from the wick and floats; or a second flame appears; or the candle vanishes; or wax appears below with no run reaching it.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The candle's colour, the holder and the surface below stay the same.
pc.fail: The candle changes colour; or the holder changes shape; or the surface below changes pattern.
